prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The positive identified set is exact only for the strengthened bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity completion class, whose simultaneous parallel-trends clause is stronger than the source's per-dose wording. The inference theorem additionally fixes a known finite rectangle union, \(\beta\), a uniform positive density lower bound, bounded outcomes, and denominator separation, and uses a conservative cell-mean radius. It proves boundary-cell coverage, signed-measure control, measurable finite-program endpoints, and ratio propagation without density smoothness, strict feasibility, or optimizer uniqueness. Because \(H\) is fixed and \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0>0\), support topology cannot approach failure within \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\). prose_updates.honest_scope: The negative conclusion is exact for the published class at the regular witness: its legal affine recession ray generates all of \(\mathbb R\), so the claimed nonparametric singleton is not identified there. The finite set \(\Theta(P)\) is instead the sharp causal set for a strengthened bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity class with a finite \(K\) movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz trends, continuous \(g\), and a simultaneous common-event diagonal clause. Marginal quasi-stayers are unnecessary for that sensitivity characterization. No global equality or inclusion with the source class is claimed, and its finite interval does not transfer upward. Baseline-conditional zero support recovers the proceedings paper's weighted singleton; arXiv:2201.06898v1 Theorem 3 concerns unweighted \(\delta_1\); and the common-zero-baseline scalar bounds in arXiv:2405.04465v4 are prior art. The source's separate parametric estimator is not challenged. Uniform outer inference is confined to the fixed known rectangle-support, fixed-H\"older, density-bounded-below, bounded-outcome, denominator-separated subclass. The established results exclude minimax lower bounds, support-topology asymptotics, unknown support, adaptive smoothness, vanishing \(A\), carry-over, clustered sampling, bounded counterfactual levels, and optimal interval length.

proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(D_I=\operatorname{diam}(I)\) and \(D_X=\operatorname{diam}(X_0)\). All constants below may depend on the fixed rectangle family, \(\beta,G,B,f_0,a_0,K,L,M,D_I\), but not on \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\).

First construct the stated boundary-aware partition. Subdivide the plane at every horizontal and vertical edge of every rectangle in \(\mathscr R\). The positive-area elementary rectangles contained in \(H\) have disjoint interiors and fixed positive side lengths. For all sufficiently small \(h_n\), subdivide an elementary side of length \(a\) into \(m=\lceil\sqrt{2}a/h_n\rceil\) equal pieces. Each resulting side lies between \(h_n/(2\sqrt{2})\) and \(h_n/\sqrt{2}\). Thus every cell has Euclidean diameter at most \(h_n\), area at least \(h_n^2/8\), and lies in a single connected component. Assign shared edges and corners by a fixed lexicographic half-open rule to a cell whose closure contains the point. Touching original rectangles cause no difficulty because rectangles sharing a boundary point are in the same connected component. This produces a deterministic Borel partition with
\[
N_n\le C_{\mathscr R}h_n^{-2}
\]
for a fixed finite constant \(C_{\mathscr R}\).

Let \(N_C\) be the sample count in a cell \(C\). The density lower bound and the area bound imply
\[
p_C=P\{(X,Z)\in C\}\ge f_0h_n^2/8.
\]
The elementary exponential-moment proof for a binomial lower tail gives
\[
P(N_C<np_C/2)\le e^{-np_C/8}
\le e^{-nf_0h_n^2/64}.
\]
Therefore, except on an event of probability at most
\[
N_ne^{-nf_0h_n^2/64}=o(1)
\]
uniformly over the class, every cell contains at least \(nf_0h_n^2/16\) observations.

Conditional on all design points, the centered variables \(\Delta Y_i-g(X_i,Z_i)\) are independent, have conditional mean zero, and lie in an interval of length at most \(4B\). The exponential-moment bound for a bounded centered variable gives, for a cell containing \(m\) observations,
\[
P\left(\left|m^{-1}\sum_{i\in C}\{\Delta Y_i-g(X_i,Z_i)\}\right|>x\ \middle|\ (X_i,Z_i)_{i=1}^n\right)
\le 2\exp\left\{-\frac{mx^2}{8B^2}\right\}.
\]
With
\[
x=2B\sqrt{\frac{128\log(8N_n/\alpha)}{nf_0h_n^2}},
\]
the count lower bound and a union bound make the conditional failure probability no larger than \(\alpha/4\). If \(w\) is assigned to \(C\), every design point in \(C\) is in the same component and within distance \(h_n\) of \(w\), including when \(w\) lies on an assigned boundary. The H\"older condition therefore gives the deterministic bias bound \(Gh_n^\beta\). We have proved
\[
P\left\{\sup_{w\in H}|\widehat g_n(w)-g(w)|\le r_n\right\}
\ge 1-\frac{\alpha}{4}-N_ne^{-nf_0h_n^2/64}
\]
uniformly over \(P\). Since \(nh_n^2/\log n\to\infty\), the last term tends to zero.

Next control the signed objective uniformly. Extend every bounded \(L\)-Lipschitz function on \(X_0\) to the convex hull of \(X_0\), retaining the same bounds and Lipschitz constant. For \(f_u(s,x)=su(x)\), symmetrization with an independent copy and independent Rademacher variables \((\eta_i)\) gives directly by conditional Jensen's inequality
\[
E\sup_u|(P_n-P)f_u|
\le 2E\sup_u\left|\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\eta_iS_i u(X_i)\right|.
\]
Conditionally on the data, \(\eta_iS_i\) are again Rademacher variables. Writing an absolutely continuous Lipschitz extension as \(u(x)=u(a)+\int_a^xu'(t)\,dt\), with \(|u(a)|\le M\) and \(|u'|\le L\), and using Cauchy--Schwarz for each Rademacher sum yields
\[
E\sup_u\left|\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\eta_iS_i u(X_i)\right|
\le \frac{M+LD_X}{\sqrt n}.
\]
Replacing one observation changes the supremum by at most \(2M/n\). Iterating the bounded-difference exponential-moment inequality therefore gives, with probability at least \(1-\alpha/2\),
\[
\sup_u|(P_n-P)f_u|
\le \frac{2(M+LD_X)}{\sqrt n}
+M\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2/\alpha)}{n}}
\le q_n.
\]
The last inequality follows from \(\log(8/\alpha)\ge\log 8\); if \(M=0\), the class contains only the zero function and the assertion is immediate. Since \(\mathcal C_P\) is a subclass, this proves the signed-measure part of \(\mathcal E_n(P)\).

The variables \(S\Delta Y\) and \(|Z|\) lie in intervals of lengths \(4B\) and \(D_I\), respectively. The same bounded exponential-moment calculation gives
\[
P(|\widehat T_n-T|>t_n)\le\alpha/8,
\qquad
P(|\widehat A_n-A|>a_n)\le\alpha/8.
\]
No independence among the four events is needed. A union bound proves
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}:\,\mathcal C_P\ne\varnothing}
P\{\text{all four bands hold}\}\ge 1-\alpha.
\]

On these bands, fix \(u\in\mathcal C_P\). Its restriction to \(\widehat B_n\) satisfies the level and pairwise Lipschitz inequalities. At every support-mesh point \((d_j,z_j)\),
\[
|\widehat g_n(d_j,z_j)-u(d_j)|
\le |\widehat g_n(d_j,z_j)-g(d_j,z_j)|+K|z_j|
\le r_n+K|z_j|.
\]
The signed and moment bands give
\[
|J_P(u)-\textstyle\int u\,d\widehat\nu_n|\le q_n,
\qquad |T-\widehat T_n|\le t_n,
\qquad |A-\widehat A_n|\le a_n.
\]
Also \(A\in[a_0,D_I]\). Hence
\[
(u|_{\widehat B_n},J_P(u),T,A)\in\widehat{\mathscr F}_n
\qquad\text{for every }u\in\mathcal C_P,
\]
so the last clause in the definition of \(\mathcal E_n(P)\) follows from the first four. We have therefore proved the advertised uniform probability bound for \(\mathcal E_n(P)\).

The preceding inclusion immediately gives coverage by the raw ratio extrema. Taking an optimizer of \(J_P\) at \(V_P^+\) and one at \(V_P^-\), whose existence follows from the compact-attainment result for \(\mathcal C_P\),
\[
\inf_{\widehat{\mathscr F}_n}\frac{t-j}{a}
\le\frac{T-V_P^+}{A},
\qquad
\sup_{\widehat{\mathscr F}_n}\frac{t-j}{a}
\ge\frac{T-V_P^-}{A}.
\]
The true interval lies in \([-K,K]\), so endpoint clipping preserves these inequalities. On \(\mathcal E_n(P)\) the feasible set is nonempty and the two raw extrema cannot cross; thus the reset rule is not invoked.

It remains to bound excess length. Take any feasible \((v,j,t,a)\). Extend the node vector to a bounded \(L\)-Lipschitz function \(E_nv\) on \(X_0\). At a support point \(w=(d,z)\), choose a same-component mesh point \(w_j=(d_j,z_j)\) within \(s_n\). The regression band, the relaxed mesh constraint, and the H\"older and Lipschitz inequalities give
\[
|g(d,z)-E_nv(d)|
\le K|z|+\varepsilon_n,
\qquad
\varepsilon_n=2r_n+(K+L)s_n+Gs_n^\beta.
\]
Because \(s_n\le h_n\) and \(r_n\ge Gh_n^\beta\),
\[
\varepsilon_n\le 3r_n+(K+L)s_n.
\]
Clipping stability supplies \(u^*=\Pi_P(E_nv)\in\mathcal C_P\) with \(\|E_nv-u^*\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_n\). Every observed \(X_i\) is a node, so \(E_nv(X_i)=v(X_i)\). Using first the program's \(j\)-constraint, then empirical total variation one, and finally the signed band for the exact feasible \(u^*\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
|j-J_P(u^*)|
&\le\left|j-\int E_nv\,d\widehat\nu_n\right|
+\left|\int(E_nv-u^*)\,d\widehat\nu_n\right|
+\left|\int u^*\,d\widehat\nu_n-J_P(u^*)\right|\\
&\le 2q_n+\varepsilon_n.
\end{aligned}
\]
Likewise \(|t-T|\le2t_n\) and \(|a-A|\le2a_n\). Since both denominators are at least \(a_0\), and since \(|(T-J_P(u^*))/A|\le K\),
\[
\left|\frac{t-j}{a}-\frac{T-J_P(u^*)}{A}\right|
\le\frac{\varepsilon_n+2q_n+2t_n+2Ka_n}{a_0}.
\]
Every feasible ratio is therefore within this distance of some point of \(\Theta(P)\). Applying the statement to minimizers and maximizers and combining it with outer inclusion proves that both endpoint gaps are nonnegative and bounded by this quantity. Because \(A\le D_I\), it is at most a fixed-class multiple of
\[
\frac{r_n+(K+L)s_n+q_n+t_n+Ka_n}{A}.
\]

For measurability, order the deterministic mesh nodes and the observed baseline coordinates lexicographically, removing duplicates by the first-index rule. This is a Borel operation. Cell counts, cell sums, and the empty-cell convention make every coefficient of the finite program Borel in \(\mathcal Z_n\). Since \(a\ge a_0>0\), set \(c=1/a\) and multiply \((v,j,t,a)\) by \(c\); the constraint \(ca=1\) and all remaining inequalities are linear, which is the stated Charnes--Cooper transformation. The transformed feasible set is a compact polytope. For fixed \(n\), enumerate its finitely many possible active-constraint bases; on each Borel determinant stratum the associated vertex is a Borel rational function of the coefficients. Taking the least objective value and then successively the least coordinate among ties selects the lexicographically least optimizer by finitely many Borel comparisons. The maximum and reset rule are handled identically. Thus \(\widehat L_n\), \(\widehat U_n\), and \(\widehat{\mathrm{CI}}_n\) are Borel measurable; no optimizer uniqueness is assumed.

Finally, \(N_n=O(h_n^{-2})\) and the declared bandwidth imply
\[
h_n^\beta
=O\!\left(\left\{\frac{\log n}{n}\right\}^{\beta/(2\beta+2)}\right),
\qquad
\sqrt{\frac{\log N_n}{nh_n^2}}
=O\!\left(\left\{\frac{\log n}{n}\right\}^{\beta/(2\beta+2)}\right).
\]
Also \(s_n\le h_n\) and \(q_n,t_n,a_n=O(n^{-1/2})\). Substitution in the endpoint bound proves the stated uniform rate. Every construction used closed inequalities and deterministic boundary assignment, so density smoothness, strict feasibility, and optimizer uniqueness were nowhere required.
